features.title: Beta Stabilization
features.summary: Keep the current page-bound Lens loop stable before inviting more users.
features.why: The v2 hypothesis depends on reliable Lens creation, anchoring, reading modes, and companion opt-in behavior.
features.resumePoint: Continue with manual smoke testing and backup/observability review before inviting more beta users.
nextActions: Run the manual smoke checklist from project status
Decide the backup and observability minimum for broader beta use
scope: Keep production API-base build guard working
Re-test companion mode after service-worker or WebSocket changes
Review open reports through the operator queue
Back up local and server data before broader beta use

updates.text: Project status moved to pre-release beta stabilization.
Added to the public roadmap as the active stabilization track.

features.title: Roadmap Page
features.summary: Expose current, next, planned, exploring, deferred, and shipped feature tracks as a lightweight docs page.
features.why: A public roadmap helps beta users and future agents see what is moving without turning planning into a heavy project-management system.
features.resumePoint: Roadmap is local/static-first, has a local stdio MCP server, and should stay out of the Lumen cloud server boundary.
nextActions: Review roadmap wording in the browser
Configure bun run mcp:roadmap in the MCP client that should read the roadmap
Keep Lumen deployment free of Roadmap runtime

updates.text: Initial roadmap data model and static page implementation started.
Added operator-only CRUD API design and implementation for roadmap features.
Roadmap Studio plan saved; public API, SQLite persistence, and operator feature CRUD moved into active development.
Added feature notebooks and generated docs/roadmap.md so fresh-context agents can resume feature work.
Removed Roadmap from the Lumen server boundary and kept it as a local/static project notebook.
Added a local stdio MCP server for roadmap resources and feature-stage update tools.

features.title: Theme System
features.summary: Switch complete Lumen UI styles through a shared theme contract, CSS variables, and generated motion profiles.
features.why: Lumen will keep adding UI and motion; a theme contract prevents future components from hardcoding one visual style.
features.resumePoint: Theme switching foundation is committed on codex/theme-switching at 9776f67. Continue by adding a compact specimen or manual visual checklist, then reduce the CSS override layer by moving core components to direct token consumption.
nextActions: Add specimen coverage or a manual visual QA checklist for orb, card, composer, InfoPanel, marker, and bloom states
Run the normal extension dev loop and inspect Classic and Signal on real pages
Refactor theme runtime application out of content.tsx only if another theme-related behavior is added
Progressively replace the post-hoc CSS override layer with direct token consumption in component styles
outOfScope: Replacing reading modes with theme choices

updates.text: Theme system design documented with a roadmap feedback contract for future implementation stages.

Committed theme switching foundation on codex/theme-switching at 9776f67: added theme profiles, stored theme preference, popup skin selector, Shadow host theme attributes, theme-aware marker styles, and theme-aware bloom generation with Classic and Signal skins.

features.title: Composer Markdown Preview
features.summary: Let Lens authors preview Markdown before publishing when longer Lens content makes that useful.
features.why: Markdown support is already useful for reading; preview may reduce publishing friction for knowledge and challenge Lens.
scope: Use the same lightweight Markdown renderer as Lens cards
outOfScope: Tables unless real usage asks for them

features.title: Cross-page Lens Reference Lookup
features.summary: Resolve `[[lens:id]]` references when the referenced Lens is not on the current page.
features.why: Lens references are first-class; cross-page lookup makes the reference graph more useful without exposing Atlas UI.

features.title: PDF Lens Surface
features.summary: Explore a PDF.js-based Lens surface for text-based PDFs using document identity and page-rectangle anchors.
features.why: PDFs are a natural reading surface for papers, manuals, and exported books, but they need a surface adapter instead of PDF branches throughout the webpage content script.
scope: Text quote and page rectangle anchors

updates.text: PDF Lens direction captured in the Lens product design and extension runtime boundary notes.

features.title: Persistent Lounge
features.summary: A durable social space may exist later, but page-bound Lens cards remain the v2 center.
features.why: Durable Lounge history could compete with Lens as the page memory before the core participation loop is validated.
scope: Revisit only after page Lens participation is stable
outOfScope: Replacing Lens cards as page memory

features.title: Atlas UI
features.summary: Atlas remains a long-term ecosystem direction, not a visible Lumen v2 UI surface.
features.why: v2 should validate contextual Lens participation before introducing knowledge graph interfaces.
scope: Keep Lens data compatible with future node candidates
Avoid exposing graph UI in v2
outOfScope: Public reputation or canonical node workflows
